requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd -m appworker succeeded (cmd-a9ff8f91d3c24c3d), confirmed via id/getent passwd showing uid=1000, home /home/appworker, shell /bin/bash both before (cmd-4aa8245e4c4c45cb) and after reboot (cmd-fcc29e758b0a47d7).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256 (cmd-a9ff8f91d3c24c3d). A genuine pam_limits login shell ('sudo -i -u appworker') reports ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256, confirmed both pre-reboot (cmd-a9ff8f91d3c24c3d, cmd-4aa8245e4c4c45cb) and post-reboot (cmd-fcc29e758b0a47d7), demonstrating both correct config and actual enforcement/persistence.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured with boot_id 83a0a80f... (cmd-4aa8245e4c4c45cb), matching the fixed before-prepare boot-identity snapshot. Restart acknowledged via shutdown -r now (cmd-77c2e2805453410d), node unreachable during transition (cmd-922b5f2c41e24cf1, cmd-21c154c6be6e431f), then reachable again with a different boot_id 1638d34f... (cmd-4141931212134f59), matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart recovery of the account, limits config, and enforced ulimits was directly re-verified (cmd-fcc29e758b0a47d7). This constitutes a complete bounded disruption-and-recovery transition.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and applied a limits.d config enforcing 8192 open files and 256 processes, verifying enforcement via a real pam_limits login shell both before and after a full node reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, distinct post-restart boot identity consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and confirmed recovery of the account and limits. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found; the only residue is a trivial reboot log file.
limitations: No probing of concurrent/simultaneous appworker sessions to confirm the nproc limit applies across multiple processes at once, though the pam_limits shell check is a standard and sufficient verification method.
The reboot log content itself (/tmp/reboot.log) was not inspected to confirm shutdown completed without errors, though the changed boot_id is direct proof of a successful restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are directly tied to task outcomes or the restart evidence protocol: useradd (required), limits.d config write (required), and shutdown -r now plus polling (restart protocol, not the public task contract but expected practice, executed safely and reverted to a healthy running state). No troubleshooting experiments, no failed/conflicting services (failed-services observation is empty in both before and after snapshots), no package-health degradation (dnf healthy both times), and no unsafe exposure changes — the only listening-socket differences are PID churn from the reboot itself, not new exposure. The lone minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a low-risk, expected artifact of the shutdown dispatch redirection, not abandoned application state.
